question.text: Per NISM Ch 2.6.1 citing SEBI circulars from 2017, Indian Category III AIFs are permitted to invest in commodity derivatives up to what proportion of investable funds in ONE underlying commodity?

answer.text: 50% of investable funds in one underlying commodity.
25% of investable funds in one underlying commodity.
10% of investable funds in one underlying commodity, subject to SEBI reporting requirements.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 2.6.1, Indian Category III AIFs are permitted by SEBI to invest in all commodity derivatives products traded on the commodity derivatives exchanges. They can invest up to 10 percent of the investable funds in one underlying commodity, subject to the reporting requirements set forth by SEBI (SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CDMRD/DMP/CIR/P/2017/61 dated June 21, 2017). The Trap: Option A is false because concentration limits exist. Options B and C are common distractor percentages used on NISM exams; candidates who don't recall the exact 10% figure drift to those values. Note: The keyed limit is 10% of investable funds per underlying commodity, paired with SEBI's reporting requirements.
